title: Zion, Jerusalem, and the Peace of Christ
english: “But I will be jealous for you.” He pre-announced these things by stirring her up, so that she would not fall to the threats, guarding the justice of the household undefiled. 1.64 Zion and Jerusalem call the one being zealously loved so that she might no longer be exhausted by those attacking her toward evils, because of the virtues having come to her. For Zion is interpreted as a lookout, a settled commandment, and Jerusalem as a vision of peace; Zion is called by upward movement the one who looks not at the temporal things but the eternal things in order to do the commandments having been given.

Following such a state is the unmixed and undisturbed nature of those succeeding. And peace is seen, that of which Jesus says: “My peace I leave to you” (John 14:27). And this is given with divine grace from God the Father and Lord Jesus Christ, as Paul teaches. And both these things, peace and grace, I say, the Savior is. For it is said concerning him: “He is our peace” (Eph 2:14). And again, he who succeeds from it and through it says: “Not I” did these certain exploits succeed, “but the grace with me” (2 Cor 12:9). This grace and peace, God the Father providing, Jesus establishes them, granting himself to partake in the grace and peace of those having known him to be. 1.66 May we also become such by good choice, so that we may not be abandoned, like a woman having dishonored her husband, becoming zealous ones desiring him.

1.67 Zach. 1:16: Because of this these things the Lord says: “I will return to Jerusalem in mercy, and my house shall be rebuilt in her,” says the Lord of hosts, “and a measuring line shall be stretched over Jerusalem still.” 1.68 Since nothing happens by chance by the one providing for all things, because of this, causal conjunctions are often placed before things happening, God saying to those subject to his administration: instead of “these things you said or did,” “these things shall be brought to you.” Immediately indeed, even in the present word, there is carried the word having this manner: “Because of this these things says the Lord of hosts.” 1.69 What is this, or the “I will be jealous for Zion and Jerusalem with great zeal” (Zechariah 1:14)? Since, “after my being angry a little, they attacked toward evils” (Zechariah 1:15) the enemies of those being envied, “I will return to Jerusalem in mercy” (Zechariah 1:16), pitying her like a protector and genuine helper, for he is a “father” to this.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Rebuilding and Measuring of Jerusalem
english: The manner of having mercy on Jerusalem is immediately announced: 'For my house shall be rebuilt in it' (Ezekiel 37:27) and in its midst, so that by dwelling and walking among its citizens, He may perfectly have mercy on it, no longer allowing it to be desolate or plundered, proving Himself a zealot and one to be remembered, stretching out a measure over it again as before when it had prosperity and fruitfulness. For a desolate and neglected land that is not being surveyed, the land being pitied by God is instead measured like a fruitful land. And the city is measured, being laid out into groves and squares, and cut into gymnasia.

What is the measure being imposed upon it in these things will be shown by an angel appearing, holding a geometric cord. The house being built in the midst of the pitied Jerusalem is the Church of the living God, in which it is fitting for the Healer of God, sanctified according to law, to dwell. This the Apostle speaking in Christ cries out to Timothy, writing thus: 'If you are delayed in seeing how one must conduct oneself in the house of God, which is the Church of the living God, a pillar and foundation of the truth' (1 Timothy 3:15).

According to another understanding, the house being rebuilt in Jerusalem, which is Jesus, who was brought forth from Mary, having been built by the wisdom of God, has according to the proverbial decree thus: 'Wisdom built a house for herself' (Proverbs 9:1), concerning which the building wisdom said to the opponents: 'Destroy this temple and in three days I will raise it up' (John 2:19); this, he says, 'was speaking about the temple of his body,' as the evangelist wrote. Regarding the things said, each of the faithful is also a house being raised up to be a temple of God. 'For do you not know, he says, that you are a temple of God, and the Spirit of God dwells in you?' (1 Corinthians 3:16). And the Savior himself says this clearly: 'If anyone loves me, he will keep my word, and I will love him, and we will come to him and make a dwelling with him' (John 14:23). A temple and a house and a dwelling: 'And the angel who was speaking with me turned and said to me, saying: Thus says the Lord of hosts: Cities shall again be scattered in prosperity, and the Lord will show mercy' (Zechariah 1:17).
the good things of the land

title: The Craftsmen of Mercy and Faith
english: Open your eyes and see: Who has demonstrated all these things? The one who leads out the world by number... and the prophet, placed for examination, lifting up his eyes to the true light, has seen... desiring to know who they are.

And the four horns lying over the citizens of Zion and Jerusalem are builders. There are no others among those enemies about whom the Apostle and the rest say: 'Our struggle is not against blood and flesh, but against the rulers and authorities and the cosmic powers of this darkness and the spiritual forces of wickedness' (Ephesians 6:12). Consistent with the multitude of the powers of the evil ones against which the struggle is for the saints, and the singer who says regarding the one overcoming the enemies: 'He shall mount upon a shield and a basilisk, and shall trample the lion and the dragon' (Psalm 91:13). And since each of the said evil ones rises tyrannically, he says they rule lawlessly.

These horns, promised through enigma, the prophet saw, lifting up the eyes of his mind, so that from having seen the preparation and the power of them, he might put on the invincible panoply of God. Who then are the builders sharpening the presented horns? It is possible to learn from the following, having such [knowledge].

Zechariah 2:2: And he said to me: These horns which scattered Judah and Israel have ascended. The responding angel, showing to the prophet the clarified four horns, the work and the need for which they were brought, says to the one being enlightened, that the horns were brought for no other reason than to scatter Israel and Judah from the holy city, so that, having been scattered into captivity, they might become outside of unity and harmony. It was said previously as Judah confessing; but he, seeing God in his mind, is called Israel.

Zechariah 2:3-4: And the Lord showed me four builders. And I said: What are these coming to do? And he said to me: These horns which scattered Judah and Israel have ascended, and none of them bowed his head; and they entered...
The four horns sharpen themselves against the nations raised against the Lord's earth, in order to scatter it.

The seer, being pleased by the multitude of approaching enemies, is shown by the one pointing out the numbers called for help that the craftsmen are praiseworthy; for not all who fashion appropriate works are praised, but some are also counterfeit, whom they send away from one another according to the proverbial rule: 'Good men fashion mercy and faith; evil craftsmen do not know mercy and faith.'

This worst workshop of the craftsmen is nothing other than the four horns, being an instrument of all unfaithfulness and crudity. Those whom God shows coming are craftsmen of mercy and faith, performing practical virtue through mercy toward neighbors, loving them as themselves, and fashioning faith through pious and scientific contemplation. No one else leads and shows to the seer the eyes of the soul, nor does God, who through doing good shows those able to help the afflicted.

Having seen those shown to him and coming by God, he asks the one showing him what they will do having come, and God answers him that they come to sharpen the nations raised against God's earth, the four [horns], in order to take the ones being handed over into captivity, so that they may scatter Judah and humble Israel, so that no one of the afflicted is able to lift up his head or defy the approaching enemies. But the word of the horns presents a greater weakness, for even after sharpening, it has not become possible for them to tear apart the ones handed over to them, even while the craftsmen who are sharpening them are present.

The word makes it manifest how the one being scattered is brought down, undergoing destruction by proximity, just as the one coming down from Jerusalem encountered spiritual robbers such that he became like a naked man to them, especially when they stripped him of the garment he had worn in the holy city, which was equal in power to weapons; the Apostle writes concerning this to those being stirred up to war: 'Put on...'
